title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Slave Knight Gael** is a character in *Dark Souls III: Ashes of Ariandel* and the final boss in *The Ringed City* DLC.

He is voiced by Stephen Boxer.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Gael was once a slave knight, an order of Undead knights who were used as fodder in the bleakest of battles. Even as they grew decrepit, their skin charred black, their bones twisted and their minds lost, they were never relieved from duty, their condemned stature signified by their vibrant red hoods. At one point, Gael managed to free himself from his life of bloody battles and ended up in the Painted World of Ariandel, a refuge for the forlorn souls who had no place to call home. There he eventually met the Painter, the "Lady" of the corvian inhabitants of the Painted World, who had extensive knowledge of the First Flame and the Dark Soul. The Painter apparently had the ability to incorporate these two concepts into creating new Painted Worlds. Gael eventually came to be a parental figure for her, such that she called him "Uncle Gael".

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - questline 
 questline : Upon arrival to the Cleansing Chapel, he will be found beside the altar, praying to who is likely Caitha. Noticing the player, he will ask if they would show his lady flame. If the player says no, he will ignore their refusal until agreed, playing a cutscene wherein he will produce a fragment of the painting for the player to enter. While this will be the last time the player sees of him for a while, he can later be summoned for the fight against Sister Friede.

When journeying to the Ringed City through the Dreg Heap, Gael will guide the Ashen One in the form of messages, encouraging them to defy common sense in several locations by taking leaps of faith. Later on, he can be summoned for the fight against the Demon Prince, the final hurdle before reaching the Ringed City.

title: Pygmy Lord
snippet:
As primordial beings predating most modern humans, they were able to better resist the effects of aging thanks to the Dark Soul that kept them alive to the point that their very blood dried out. The wizened Slave Knight Gael, who sought the Dark Soul with the goal of taking it to his Lady, devoured them and their viscous blood rich of the Dark Soul, even though he was quite aware of the negative effects it would inflict, for he was not a champion fit to receive its full power.

As the last survivor of Gael's massacre, he attempts to make it to Filianore's remains even with his throat slashed by Gael, and his legs bleeding and broken. The Ashen One would pass by the pitiful soul, who would never get to see the princess' final state, succumbing to his wounds as he called out her name in vain.

title: Dark Soul
snippet: Near the end of the Age of Fire, a slave knight called Gael traveled to the Ringed City, seeking the Pygmy Lords to gain their blood. The blood of the Dark Soul was intended to be used to paint a new Painted World, but to Gael's shock, Filianore's spell was broken and the Pygmy Lords were aged to the point that their blood did not flow, for it was dried in their veins. Even though he knew he had not the strength to survive bearing it, Gael slew the Pygmy Lords and drank from their wounds, absorbing the Dark Soul into himself. It imbued him with a dark miasma and warped his mind, but in the end he was successful, slain by the Ashen One to extract the soul's blood. The current state of the Dark Soul is unknown, but given the eternal nature of Lord Souls, it is unlikely that it was truly destroyed.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : Gael cannot be permanently killed as a character. He will always respawn in the Cleansing Chapel (may take several reloads).
Gael's summon sign for fighting Sister Friede is unique in that it can be used even if not embered; moreover, he will be summoned directly into the arena, not at his summoning sign, and only when the second phase of the fight commences. He is the only character in the franchise to have a summon sign that functions this way. It also can be used if all your phantom summons are filled up even with the Dried Finger, allowing for a boss fight with 4 phantoms. Furthermore, this summon does not increase Friede's health, similarly to Great Grey Wolf Sif's summon in *Dark Souls I* for Manus, Father of the Abyss.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet:
Sometime before the arrival of the Ashen One at the Ringed City, a pygmy—plausibly a disgruntled Pygmy Lord— came to detest the Gods for condemning the pygmies to their accursed fate, and took up residence at the outskirts of their city. There, he welcomed new arrivals and directed into Filianore's Church those who sought the Dark Soul, where they could confront the "lid covering an overgrown privy".

The Pygmy Lords obeyed and relied on the gods for eons, and remained passive unto the end of time, at which point even their own blood had dried up. The last Pygmy Lords would meet their ends at the hands of Slave Knight Gael, who had sought their Dark Soul for centuries. Finding that their blood had long ago dried up, he consumed their Dark Soul, so that he could take it back to his Lady to be used as pigment for her painting.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: Nevertheless, the tales of the painting also told of a prophecy: "When the Ashes are two, a flame alighteth". If another Ash were to enter the Painting, there would yet be hope to kindle the flame and burn the rotten world away. And so Gael fled the Painted World, taking with him a rotten scrap of it, to seek out another Unkindled who could show Flame to his Lady. After a long, unsuccessful search, Gael would find himself in the Cleansing Chapel where he laid prostrate before a shrine to Caitha, mother of the forlorn, praying that his wish be granted by the goddess. This was where Gael finally encountered the Ashen One during their journey through Lothric, and managed to convince them to touch the scrap of painting, transporting them to the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Gael's facial data, including his beard, is unique to him and is not available as an option when creating the player's character.
Impaling the corpse of a Pygmy lord with his sword and tossing it at the player is a reference to Knight Artorias, who performs a similar act at the start of his boss fight, and to the Penetrator before him in *Demon's Souls*.
Out of any boss from the entire franchise, Gael has the biggest boss arena, as the Pygmy's Throne is a completely explorable desert-like zone.
The way Gael moves and fights on the first phase is very similar to how Guts, from the *Berserk* anime/manga, does when using the Berserker Armor. In the second phase, the Repeating Crossbow is also reminiscent of Guts' Repeater Crossbow and the way he hides and follows his attacks with a cape.
A summon sign appears beneath Gael wherever he reappears at when he teleports during his boss fight.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: Gael's mission was therefore not over, and so the knight set off again with a new mission: to find the Dark Soul and bring it back to the Painter so she could complete her painting. He knew that he lacked a Champion's strength, that bearing the Dark Soul would likely ruin and consume him, leaving him scant hope of safe return; nonetheless, he set out on his endless journey, crossing the centuries through countless battles and hardships. His Executioner's Greatsword remained with him from beginning to end, becoming heavily chipped and stained with blood, and the Repeating Crossbow he customized was rusted with blood, overused, twisted and marred with dents and scratches. Gael's own body too suffered from the long journey, being consumed by the ever-expanding Darksign that fused his flesh with his now rusted and cracked armor.

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: Some of the dethroned god's followers, now cast out from the reformed faith, would find refuge in the Painted World of Ariandel, bringing with them the lost miracles of the old religion and fully believing that one day the aureoles of light associated with Lloyd would return with him. It's possible that Slave Knight Gael was once such a believer, due to his usage of that very miracle. That is in spite of his nature as a cursed Undead, which the old god seemingly despised.

snippet: On their quest, the Ashen One encounters the Painted World of Ariandel, and a little girl whose duty it is to become the new Painter, and replace it with a fresh, unrotted version. To do this, she reveals that she needs the blood of the bearer of the Dark Soul, and that her guardian Gael has gone to find it. At the end of time, as the flames are reduced to embers and sparks, the entire world has begun to collapse in on itself, surrounding the ageless Ringed City. title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
She will have some extra dialogue if the player has joined the Spears of the Church covenant, commending them on their choice to serve Princess Filianore. However, Shira will become permanently hostile if her slumber is disturbed, disappearing from all her previous locations, halting her involvement in the Midir sideplot. She will ambush the player in a delapitated ruin found in the ashen desert accessed from the Filianore's Rest bonfire. While battling the player, the Slave Knight Gael fight won't begin. Conversely, if his boss fight has already started, she will not show up at her spot. She'll still attack the player even after his defeat.

Slaying her here will net her Crucifix of the Mad King as well as any item she could have gifted but hadn't yet. The door from which you could speak to her before will also be open, revealing a corpse holding the entirety of her set.

snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - the_painted_world_of_ariandel 
 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Sir Vilhelm
snippet:
At some point, the Ashen One is beckoned to the Painted World of Ariandel by Slave Knight Gael, who believed they are the Ash meant to defeat the other Ash currently ruling over the painted landscape. The first meeting appears to be cordial, with Vilhelm pointing them to Friede, and then reinforcing her sentiment about them leaving the world behind and getting back to their journey. He also warns them to suppress their curiosity, as the depths of the painting would easily destroy them in their endeavors to sate it.

When encountered in the building housing the captive painter girl, he will deride the Ashen One's inquisitiveness, claiming he has seen their type often and that they would never have what it takes to actually face the danger they have put themselves in by sticking their nose where it didn't belong. After a duel to the death, the Unkindled champion is victorious, slaying Vilhelm, who laments his failure to uphold his oath to Friede.

snippet:
Possibly due to the gruesome rituals within the Cathedral, the waters of the Deep were over time corrupted, with the dregs from its depths birthing abominations. The clerics of the Cathedral were haunted with visions of an encroaching darkness, sparking a wave of change in their faith. Led by the visionary cleric Aldrich and the three archdeacons, they abandoned their faith in Caitha, covering up most of her statues, and deemed her chimes anathema, hiding them away.

Within the Cleansing Chapel neighboring the Cathedral, Slave Knight Gael can be found on his knees praying to one of the covered statues of the weeping maiden, calling out to her as a "merciful goddess" and "mother of the forlorn, who have no place to call their own". Whether Gael refers to Caitha herself, or if he, in his madness, glimpsed the likeness of the beloved mistress of his cold home, is unknown.

title: The Deep
snippet:
It is unclear what would have become of Aldrich at the end of the Age of Fire. While the champion of the Deep has already been defeated when the Ashen One visits the Ringed City or the Dreg Heap, it seems that his visions of an incoming Age of Deep Sea were close to coming to pass, with the remnants of the world of Man bustling with the sunken, stagnated dregs of humanity, the malformed legacy of the Dark Soul which had been suppressed by the Darksign for millennia.

To prevent the advent of the Age of Deep following the weakening of the First Flame, the plan of the Sable Church of Londor has become to tear the Flame off its Kiln and preserve it within a Lord of Hollows who can exploit its power, freezing the state of the world thanks to their Dark Sigil.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Once arriving at the Dragon Shrine bonfire, the Scholar appears once more. He will reveal that he is in fact Aldia, the elder brother of Vendrick. Aldia says that he "sought to shed the yoke of fate, but failed" and that he now only awaits an answer. He asks of the Bearer of the Curse to "seek the Throne, seek light, dark and what lies beyond", for the last time, he'll vanish into the flames, allowing the Bearer of the Curse to light the bonfire.

The Ancient Dragon will give the Bearer the Ashen Mist Heart, which allows one to peer into the memories of things long withered. Should the Bearer of the Curse again seek out Nashandra's council, she will warn that the dragon is a false deity and is in fact no more than a prop. Still, she will direct the Bearer of the Curse to go to the Forest of Fallen Giants, to use the Ashen Mist Heart to peer into the Giants' memories.

title: The Dreg Heap
snippet:
The Dreg Heap -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Found at the world's end, the Dreg Heap is the result of the close of the Age of Fire: with the world collapsing in on itself, ancient lands and ancient civilizations all find themselves converging into a single location. Among the remnants of old cilizations that converged onto the Dreg Heap are the windmill from Drangleic's Earthen Peak.

At the start of the area, an unnamed pilgrim of Londor watches over the merging of the kingdoms, musing over the end of the known world. The early areas of the Heap are populated by many Murkmen spawning from the ground, and flying over the area are powerful Angels manifested by the much-weaker, hiding Pilgrim Pupas.

A poisonous swamp is found deeper down, atop which Desert Pyromancer Zoey, a descendant of the Desert Sorceresses of Drangleic, acts as queen to the Thralls found within.

title: Ashen One
snippet: The Ashen One defeats Gael, and gains the Blood of the Dark Soul. They may then return this to the Painter, who states that she will use the Blood of the Dark Soul to paint a new Painted World. She offers to name it after the Ashen One, and if the Ashen One gives no name, she states that she will name it the Painted World of Ash.

title: The Dreg Heap
snippet:
The Dreg Heap -  Dark Souls III - location - accessing_the_dreg_heap 
 accessing_the_dreg_heap : There are two ways of accessing the Dreg Heap:

Should the player defeat the Twin Princes and place all four Cinders of a Lord upon their thrones at Firelink Shrine, the player will be able to access the Kiln of the First Flame. After proceeding to the Kiln from the Flameless Shrine, there will be a bonfire adjacent to the Kiln bonfire, with a tattered strip of Slave Knight Gael's cape affixed to the hilt. Accessing this bonfire will warp the player to the Dreg Heap.

Alternatively, if the player owns Ashes of Ariandel, they may defeat Sister Friede. Adjacent to the bonfire which appears after her defeat, a similar bonfire to the above will spawn at the back of the arena. This bonfire will also warp the player to the Dreg Heap.

title: Ammunition (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
***Duration**: time it takes for the projectile to despawn naturally.
***Initial Speed (Horizontal and Vertical)**: initial speed at which it moves, for aimed projectiles, the Vertical speed tends to start at 0.
***Acceleration Delay (Horizontal and Vertical)**: an amount of time the projectile can exist before changing either movement speed value.
***Speed Difference**(**Horizontal and Vertical**): the amount of speed the projectile will gain/lose, starting at the end of the Acceleration Delay and ending at the limit of their Duration.
***Maximum Speed (Horizontal and Vertical)**: the maximum speed the projectile can move at, often unused as the Speed Difference usually doesn't increase the speed past this number. In cases it is used, the projectile will accelerate as normal but stay at its maximum speed once it reaches it.
***Effective Range**: distance from where the player is where the damage starts to reduce, continuing to decrease until another limit.

 general_information : Each Ammunition type corresponds directly to a weapon class that can use them. Arrows work with Bows, Bolts work with Crossbows and Greatarrows work with Greatbows.

When a bow or crossbow is readied, pressing the weak attack button ( or ) will use the ammunition equipped in the first (left) slot, while pressing the strong attack button ( or ) will use the ammunition equipped in the second (right) slot.

Arrows may only be fired by bows, while bolts can only be fired by crossbows. Greatarrows, on the other hand, can only be fired by greatbows. Greatarrows may be equipped in the same slot as regular arrows.

Equipping arrows or bolts in the left equip slot while a bow or crossbow is also equipped, will cause a quiver or bolt quiver to appear on the player. Having the right slot filled but the left slot empty will not cause any quivers to appear.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Anor Londo (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Unlike its Dark Souls counterpart, Anor Londo's illusionary shining sun is gone and has been replaced with the cold blue rays of the moon. The city has noticeably frozen over, as well as being severely reduced in size, with the only remaining parts of the old city being the cathedral, the rotating staircase, and the honorary tomb of Gwyn. An additional tower now stands where the entrance of the building housing the Painted World of Ariamis once stood, with an invisible walkway leading to the top. Additionally, only three of the Silver Knights remain and all Batwing Demons are gone. The cathedral has been overrun by Deacons of the Cathedral of the Deep and Writhing Rotten Flesh. The inside of the cathedral has been covered in corpses and maggots. The eastern section of the cathedral has been blocked off by debris, but the western section is still accessible and contains the body of an old blacksmith.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

 characteristics : Like other light cloth sets, the Antiquated Set possesses very low physical absorption but very strong elemental defenses. In particular, its Fire absorption is among the highest among all light armor sets, and even competes with heavyweight titans while weighing nowhere near as much. It also has very strong Curse buildup mitigation, which is more than twice as high as its next highest resistance.

Of particular note of this set is that it includes the Crown of Dusk, which boosts the power of Magic damage-dealing spells and weaponry at the cost of a heavy Magic absorption penalty. This makes it a very popular headpiece for builds that utilize Sorceries.
